L211: ## File Names, Command Line Arguments, and Environment Variables
L212: 
L213: In Python, file names, command line arguments, and environment variables are represented using the string type. On some systems, decoding these strings to and from bytes is necessary before passing them to the operating system. Python uses the :term:`filesystem encoding and error handler` to perform this conversion (see :func:`sys.getfilesystemencoding`).
L214: The :term:`filesystem encoding and error handler` are configured at Python startup by the :c:func:`PyConfig_Read` function: see :c:member:`~PyConfig.filesystem_encoding` and :c:member:`~PyConfig.filesystem_errors` members of :c:type:`PyConfig`.
L215: 
L216:     .. versionchanged:: 3.1
L217:        On some systems, conversion using the file system encoding may fail. In this
L218:        case, Python uses the :ref:`surrogateescape encoding error handler
L219:        <surrogateescape>`, which means that undecodable bytes are replaced by a
L220:        Unicode character U+DC\ *xx* on decoding, and these are again
L221:        translated to the original byte on encoding.
L222: The :term:`file system encoding <filesystem encoding and error handler>` must guarantee to successfully decode all bytes below 128. If the file system encoding fails to provide this guarantee, API functions can raise :exc:`UnicodeError`.
L223: 
L224: See also the :term:`locale encoding`.
L225: ## Python UTF-8 Mode
L226: 
L227:     .. versionadded:: 3.7
L228:        See :pep:`540` for more details.
L229: 
L230: 
L231: 
L232:     .. versionchanged:: 3.15
L233: 
L234:        Python UTF-8 mode is now enabled by default (:pep:`686`).
L235:        It may be disabled by setting :envvar:`PYTHONUTF8=0 <PYTHONUTF8>` as
L236:        an environment variable or by using the :option:`-X utf8=0 <-X>` command line option.
L237: 
L238: 
L239: 
L240: The Python UTF-8 Mode ignores the :term:`locale encoding` and forces the usage of the UTF-8 encoding:
L241:   * Use UTF-8 as the :term:`filesystem encoding <filesystem encoding and error handler>`.
L242:   * :func:`sys.getfilesystemencoding` returns `'utf-8'`.
L243:   * :func:`locale.getpreferredencoding` returns `'utf-8'` (the do_setlocale argument has no effect).
L244:   * :data:`sys.stdin`, :data:`sys.stdout`, and :data:`sys.stderr` all use UTF-8 as their text encoding, with the `surrogateescape` :ref:`error handler <error-handlers>` being enabled for :data:`sys.stdin` and :data:`sys.stdout` (:data:`sys.stderr` continues to use `backslashreplace` as it does in the default locale-aware mode)
L245:   * On Unix, :func:`os.device_encoding` returns `'utf-8'` rather than the device encoding.
L246: Note that the standard stream settings in UTF-8 mode can be overridden by :envvar:`PYTHONIOENCODING` (just as they can be in the default locale-aware mode).
L247: 
L248: As a consequence of the changes in those lower level APIs, other higher level APIs also exhibit different default behaviours:
L249:   * Command line arguments, environment variables and filenames are decoded to text using the UTF-8 encoding.
L250:   * :func:`os.fsdecode` and :func:`os.fsencode` use the UTF-8 encoding.
L251:   * :func:`open`, :func:`io.open`, and :func:`codecs.open` use the UTF-8 encoding by default. However, they still use the strict error handler by default so that attempting to open a binary file in text mode is likely to raise an exception rather than producing nonsense data.
L252: The :ref:`Python UTF-8 Mode <utf8-mode>` is enabled by default. It can be disabled using the :option:`-X utf8=0 <-X>` command line option or the :envvar:`PYTHONUTF8=0 <PYTHONUTF8>` environment variable. The Python UTF-8 Mode can only be disabled at Python startup. Its value can be read from :data:`sys.flags.utf8_mode <sys.flags>`.
L253: If the UTF-8 mode is disabled, the interpreter defaults to using the current locale settings, unless the current locale is identified as a legacy ASCII-based locale (as described for :envvar:`PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE`), and locale coercion is either disabled or fails. In such legacy locales, the interpreter will default to enabling UTF-8 mode unless explicitly instructed not to do so.
L254: 
L255: See also the :ref:`UTF-8 mode on Windows <win-utf8-mode>` and the :term:`filesystem encoding and error handler`.
